title: Cell Structure and Organelles
notes: Cell theory: living things are made of cells, the cell is the unit of structure and function, and cells arise from cells.
A prokaryotic cell has a nucleoid, 70S ribosomes and no mitochondria. A eukaryotic cell has a nucleus and membrane-bound organelles.
The plasma membrane is a selective boundary. The cell wall, in plants, is outside it and is cellulose. Animal cells have no cellulose wall.
Mitochondria release energy by aerobic respiration and carry a little of their own DNA. Chloroplasts, in green cells, do the same kind of semi-independent life for photosynthesis.
Rough endoplasmic reticulum carries ribosomes and helps make proteins. The Golgi body packages secretions. Lysosomes hold digestive enzymes. Ribosomes, 80S in the eukaryotic cytosol, build proteins.
The nucleus holds the chromosomes. Cilia and flagella move a cell or the fluid past it. Vacuoles and stored granules are inclusions, not the same thing as an organelle with a job in metabolism.
importantConcepts: Cell membrane: selectively permeable phospholipid bilayer
Nucleus: controls cell activities, contains DNA
Mitochondria: powerhouse of the cell (ATP production)
Ribosomes: protein synthesis machinery (70S in prokaryotes, 80S in eukaryotes)
Endoplasmic reticulum: RER (protein synthesis), SER (lipid synthesis)
Golgi apparatus: modification, sorting, and packaging of proteins/lipids
Lysosomes: digestive compartments containing hydrolytic enzymes
Chloroplasts: site of photosynthesis (plant cells only)
Centrosome: organizes microtubules in animal cells
importantStatements: The cell membrane regulates what enters and exits the cell via passive and active transport.
Mitochondria generate ATP through oxidative phosphorylation in the electron transport chain.
Eukaryotic cells are larger (10-100 µm) than prokaryotic cells (1-10 µm).
Ribosomes are the sites of protein synthesis, translating mRNA into polypeptide chains.
keyPoints: Organelles have specific functions: nucleus (control), mitochondria (energy), ER (synthesis), Golgi (packaging), lysosomes (digestion).
Prokaryotic cells lack membrane-bound organelles but have a nucleoid region with DNA.
Eukaryotic cells have a true nucleus surrounded by a nuclear envelope.
specialNotes: The cell membrane is fluid mosaic model – a dynamic arrangement of lipids and proteins.
Mitochondrial DNA is circular and similar to bacterial DNA, supporting endosymbiotic theory.
Chloroplasts contain thylakoids where light-dependent reactions occur.
examShortTricks: Cell membrane is selectively permeable – small molecules diffuse freely, large molecules need carriers.
Mitochondria = powerhouse of the cell (produces ATP).
Ribosomes are found on rough ER and free in cytoplasm.
Chloroplasts are only in plant cells and algae.
examNotes: Cell theory has three postulates: 1) All living things are made of cells, 2) Cells are the basic unit of structure/function, 3) New cells come from existing cells.
Organelle function questions commonly appear – match organelle to its primary function.
Compare prokaryotic vs eukaryotic cell structures in exam questions.

mcs.question: Which organelle produces ATP?
mcs.explanation: Mitochondria are known as the powerhouses of the cell because they generate ATP through oxidative phosphorylation.

mcs.question: What is the function of the rough endoplasmic reticulum?
mcs.explanation: The rough ER has ribosomes attached and is responsible for synthesizing and transporting proteins.

mcs.question: Why do mitochondria have their own DNA?
mcs.explanation: Mitochondrial DNA is circular and similar to bacterial DNA, supporting the endosymbiotic theory where mitochondria originated from free-living bacteria.

mcs.question: What is the difference between prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells?
mcs.explanation: Eukaryotic cells have a true nucleus enclosed by a nuclear membrane, while prokaryotic cells lack this compartment.

confusion: Animal cells have no cellulose wall.
80S ribosomes are eukaryotic. 70S are prokaryotic, and also inside mitochondria.
A lysosome is not the nucleus.
Inclusions are storage. Organelles do the metabolic work.

exercises.question: Name two organelles that contain their own DNA, and one structure animal cells lack.
steps: Animal cells lack a cellulose cell wall.
Both organelles are eukaryotic, not bacterial.
exercises.answer: Mitochondria and chloroplasts. Animals lack a cellulose wall.

summary: Cells come from cells. Prokaryotes keep a nucleoid and 70S ribosomes. Eukaryotes add a nucleus, mitochondria, and, in green cells, chloroplasts, plus ER, Golgi, lysosomes and 80S ribosomes. Plants add a cellulose wall that animals do not have.
